newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM Q1 PROFITS SEEN LARGELY FLAT.
newsitem.headline: DSM Q1 PROFITS SEEN LARGELY FLAT.

text.p: High prices for plastics raw materials in the first two months of 1997 are seen pressuring first-quarter results at Dutch petrochemicals group DSM, but analysts are divided on the overall impact on the bottom line.

A Reuter poll showed analysts' forecasts of first-quarter net profit from ordinary operations range from 185-233 million guilders, with consensus at 216.8 million. DSM is due to report its figures on Tuesday.
Last year, DSM posted first-quarter net from ordinary operations of 216 million before the deduction of a one million guilder minority charge and a 10 million guilder one-off loss.
"I expect some pressure on margins, particularly in the cyclically sensitive hydrocarbons and polymers activities," said Nils van Elzelingen of NIB Securities.
He said that while sales prices for plastics had risen, this would have been countered by high prices for naphtha, a raw material, which only started falling in late February.
Van Elzelingen said he was expecting first quarter ordinary net to come in at 214 million guilders.
ING Barings' Quirijn Mulder was far more upbeat, however, forecasting first-quarter net from ordinary operations of 237 million guilders.

"Naphtha prices started falling later in the quarter, while selling prices were consistently higher than in the previous quarter," he said. Currency effects would also have boosted operating earnings, he added.

DSM does not publish a breakdown of results per sector in its quarterly report, but analysts were agreed that the biggest influence on group earnings would be the developments at its core hydrocarbons and polymers activities.
The other divisions (industrial and fine chemicals, resins and plastic products and energy) will largely have performed in line with previous quarters, they said.
